standard.title: Algorithms for Congruence and Similarity
standard.description: design, create and test algorithms involving a sequence of steps and decisions that identify congruency or similarity of shapes, and describe how the algorithm works
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have designed classification algorithms for shapes (from AC9M7SP04). Students know the conditions for congruence and similarity (from AC9M8SP01).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students design, test and describe algorithms (flowcharts or pseudocode) that classify triangles as congruent, similar, or neither, based on given measurements.

nodes.label: Designing a congruence/similarity classification algorithm
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students design a step-by-step algorithm that correctly classifies two triangles as congruent, similar, or neither, using the appropriate conditions.
nodes.minimum_width: Design a flowchart that correctly classifies two triangles as congruent or not using at least two conditions (SSS and SAS).
nodes.typical_width: Design and test an algorithm covering all congruence and similarity conditions; handle edge cases (e.g. insufficient information); describe how the algorithm works.
wider: Evaluate two different algorithms for the same classification task — compare their efficiency and edge case handling.
Extend the algorithm to classify quadrilaterals as congruent or similar — identify what additional conditions are needed.

response_modes.reason: Algorithm design requires systematic reasoning about decision order — which condition to test first, what information is needed, and how to handle each branch. Without explicit structure students produce incomplete or ambiguous algorithms.

nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires tracing and evaluating an algorithm — students who have not designed one themselves lack the understanding of decision branching and condition ordering needed to identify errors or describe logic in Node 2.
success_criteria: Designs an algorithm that correctly classifies triangles using at least two conditions.
Includes clear decision points with yes/no branches.
Tests the algorithm with at least two examples and corrects any errors.

nodes.label: Evaluating and describing algorithms
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students trace through a given algorithm with test cases, identify errors or limitations, and describe in plain language how it works.
nodes.minimum_width: Trace a given congruence/similarity algorithm with two test inputs; identify whether the algorithm is correct.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate a given algorithm for completeness and accuracy; fix identified errors; describe the algorithm's decision logic in plain language.
wider: Implement a classification algorithm in a simple programming language — test it with generated sets of triangle measurements.
Investigate: what is the minimum number of decision steps needed to distinguish all five outcomes (SSS congruent, SAS congruent, AAS congruent, RHS congruent, similar, neither)?

response_modes.reason: Evaluating an algorithm requires simultaneously applying geometric knowledge, logical reasoning, and computational thinking — an integration of the space and digital strands.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Minimising decision steps and implementing the algorithm in code are rich computational thinking extensions — advancing students who investigate algorithmic efficiency are engaging with genuine computer science concepts within the Year 8 band.
success_criteria: Correctly traces an algorithm with given inputs.
Identifies at least one error or limitation in a given algorithm.
Describes the algorithm's logic in plain language.
